summary: FlameAtlas is an AI dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion experiments into something anyone can explore in seconds. Instead of digging through scattered datasets and papers, you open one page: every experiment is summarised with its key numbers and percentages, a graph view shows how experiments, fuels and conditions connect to each other, and a search box lets you ask a question in plain English and get an answer drawn only from NASA's data. It addresses the Flame in Freefall challenge by making flame behaviour in microgravity easy to understand for students, researchers and the public. This matters because how fire behaves without gravity is a real safety question for every crewed mission, and the data that answers it should be easy to reach.
details:
FlameAtlas has three parts. Experiment summaries give each microgravity combustion experiment a short, clear summary with its main results and percentages. A graph view links experiments, fuels and test conditions so patterns across experiments are visible at a glance. An AI search box answers plain English questions using only NASA's data, so it does not invent results.

It helps students learn how flames behave in space without reading dozens of papers, and helps researchers spot links between experiments faster. Because it runs on public NASA data, it can grow as new experiments are released. I plan to keep developing it and offer it to NASA as a volunteer contribution.

It is a web app that uses an AI language model for search and summaries. I built it as a solo team, kept the interface simple for non experts, and used free tools only. AI tools assisted with the code, and the demo video's voice over is AI generated.
